newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Killer typhoid breaks out in Tajik capital.
newsitem.headline: Killer typhoid breaks out in Tajik capital.

text.p: At least 10 people have died and thousands have been infected in an outbreak of typhoid fever in the capital of the troubled Central Asian state of Tajikistan, aid officials said.

The regional delegation of the Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), warning that tens of thousands are at risk, called late on Wednesday for urgent steps to stop it spreading.
"Already, some 3,000 cases of typhoid fever have been reported but health authorities in Dushanbe are forecasting a ten-fold increase in the coming weeks," it said in a statement.
"At least 10 people have died. The disease is spead mainly through contaminated water supplies in the city," it added.

Tajikistan, ravaged by four years of civil war, is one of the poorest republics of the former Soviet Union. Many of its 5.7 million people have a limited diet and sanitary conditions are often poor, leading to outbreaks of infectious diseases.

The statement said the IFRC had started distributing much needed food and soap to Dushanbe hospitals and three tonnes of chlorine had been given to the municipal authorities to clean up the city's water supply.

On Tuesday, gunmen killed seven people in a spate of attacks in Dushanbe a day after a guerrilla group released hostages, including foreigners, whom they had held for two weeks outside the capital. Five of those shot were ethnic Russians. Moscow has thousands of peacekeeping troops in the volatile country.
